findings.detail: Informational, not a required change. The register contract was intentionally changed to match Figma (OPTION B, parent-approved): RegisterPayload/createRegisterSchema dropped email/password/confirmPassword and now collect firstName/secondName/thirdName/lastName/phone (Egyptian mobile)/nationalId (14 digits)/role. This is correct against the two sign-up nodes (221:1217 identity step, 89:4922 role step), which genuinely collect no credentials, and the user's #1 priority is exact Figma parity. Login and forgot-password logic/exports are untouched. The only residue is that the general sign-up now has no credential-collection screen and the unused email/password/confirmPassword i18n keys remain for a likely follow-up credentials step; worth a follow-up task if the backend still requires credentials at registration, but out of scope here.

summary: APPROVED. The prior blocking issue — the whole-page RTL column mirror (hero rendered right / card left under the default Arabic locale) — is fixed in commit 7a0b601: the shell row is forced dir="ltr" so the hero stays LEFT and the auth card RIGHT in every locale, matching Figma nodes 47:3798, 89:4922, and 221:1217, while the card column restores dir={getDirection(locale)} so its internals (text, fields, icons) remain RTL for Arabic. Pixel fidelity is otherwise sound: the shared split-screen shell, Login (47:3798), multi-step Sign Up (89:4922 role + 221:1217 identity), and Forgot Password compose the existing design-system atoms/molecules (Input, Button, Label, SelectableCardGroup, PasswordToggle, Email/Password/Person/Phone/CardId/role/brand icons, LogoMark) without inline-restyling them, with card-auth tokens defined for both light and dark. Auth logic and contracts are preserved where the design allows: Login (RHF + createLoginSchema + useLogin + email/password/rememberMe) and Forgot Password are intact, and the public barrel is extended (ForgotPasswordForm, createForgotPasswordSchema, types) without removing exports. The register schema/payload change that drops credentials is a deliberate, parent-approved Figma-first decision and is recorded as informational only. next-intl ar/en parity holds exactly (52/52 auth keys identical; parity test green), only logical properties are used (no left/right/ml/pl/text-left/text-right in the changed files), and a bundled token refactor splitting --input into a neutral border plus a new --input-filled is self-consistent and preserves the filled input's exact color. Gates verified on the current tree: typegen, typecheck, lint, auth schema tests (11/11), and messages-parity (1/1) all pass. No blocking concerns remain.
